name: CXL memory expanders are not a consumer path to more inference RAM - host root-port support is server-only
symptom: A tempting path for '70B fits but decode is slow' builds is to bolt on CXL memory. It cannot be done: all shipping CXL expanders (Marvell Structera X 2404/2504/3406/3506, Astera Leo 2 / Leo X, Samsung CMM, XCENA MX1) are E3.S/E3.C PCIe-CEM modules sold to server OEMs, not retail; and CXL 2.0+ requires the CPU/root-complex to enable it - consumer Intel/AMD boards do not expose CXL on their PCIe root ports.
root_cause: CXL.mem is a capacity fabric, not a bandwidth fabric. One PCIe 5.0 x16 CXL link is ~64 GB/s - WORSE than a single DDR5 channel pair - and adds ~200-400 ns over local DRAM. For bandwidth-bound LLM decode it does not help tok/s at all; for capacity it enumerates as nothing without host CXL support, which only Sapphire Rapids / Genoa-and-newer server platforms provide - and those already have 8-12 DDR5 channels so the expander is redundant.
workaround: Drop the CXL-expander plan entirely for consumer/homelab builds. If you need capacity beyond what DDR channels give you, the working paths are: fully populate a server platform's channels (see gotcha-cpu-inference-must-populate-all-memory-channels), use unified memory (Apple Silicon, Strix Halo), or spread across multiple GPUs. Revisit CXL only when consumer chipsets ship CXL root ports - no earlier than ~2027 and that is optimistic.
notes: From the big-memory research sweep: every shipping expander targets hyperscaler DDR-reclamation (Marvell Structera X 3506 = 6x DDR5 ch / up to 6TB per controller, sold to server OEMs). The ~$1,000+ OEM card put in a consumer board enumerates as nothing. CXL's one real future use is cheap far-memory so a 400B model LOADS, with a GPU doing decode from fast memory - not a decode-speed play. Bandwidth identity: cxl-2-0 == pcie-gen5 == 63 GB/s per direction; see data/interconnect/cxl-*.json.
